question: Where do school health programs mainly take place?
explanation: You got it! School health programs focus on schools because that's where children spend most of their day learning and growing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h1)

question: How do school health programs help students do better in their studies?

options.A: By guaranteeing admission to higher education
options.B: By replacing traditional classroom teaching hours
options.C: By eliminating the need for private tutoring
options.D: By reducing absences caused by preventable illnesses

explanation: Spot on! When kids are healthy and miss fewer classes due to preventable sicknesses, they stay on top of their lessons. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard school health program?
explanation: Correct! Brain surgery is specialized hospital care, way beyond what a primary school health program needs or does. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h2)

question: Why is staff wellness included as a key part of school health programs?

options.A: Teachers serve as role models whose health habits influence students
options.B: Teachers are legally required to pass annual fitness tests
options.C: School staff require more medical leave than regular workers
options.D: Staff members pay for the maintenance of school clinics

explanation: You nailed it! Children copy the adults around them, so healthy teachers naturally encourage good habits in their pupils. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h2)

question: What is a major danger of having bad sanitation and broken toilets in a school?

options.A: Rapid spread of infectious diseases like cholera
options.B: Immediate decline in mathematical reasoning skills
options.C: Permanent loss of hearing acuity in students
options.D: Sudden increase in genetic disorders among pupils

explanation: Correct! Dirty surroundings and unsafe water easily lead to water-borne illnesses and tummy infections among children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h3)

question: A school nurse notices students aren't washing their hands after using the toilet because there's no soap. What should be done right away?

options.A: Punish students who fail to wash their hands with clean water
options.B: Ensure handwashing stations are immediately stocked with soap and water
options.C: Close the school until the local government builds new toilets
options.D: Advise parents to keep their children away from school permanently

explanation: Well done! Fixing the lack of soap removes the barrier so students can easily practice good hygiene. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h3)

question: Why do routine medical checks in schools help find vision and hearing issues early?

options.A: Teachers are trained ophthalmologists and audiologists
options.B: Children rarely complain about mild sensory deficits on their own
options.C: Parents deliberately hide medical test results from school authorities
options.D: Sensory problems only develop while children are inside classrooms

explanation: Exactly! Kids often think everyone sees or hears just like they do, so they won't realize they have a problem unless we check. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h4)

question: Which tool is commonly used to check distant vision during routine school health checks?
explanation: You got it! The Snellen chart with rows of letters is the classic tool for checking how well school children can see from a distance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h4)

question: Why are role-playing and peer education so effective in school health classes?

options.A: Students prefer playing games over reading textbooks
options.B: Interactive methods remove the need for qualified teachers
options.C: Government policies ban traditional classroom lecturing
options.D: Health habits are behavioral and require active practice

explanation: Spot on! Health education is all about changing daily actions, which works best when students actually practice what they are learning. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h5)

question: What should health education focus on most for younger primary school children?

options.C: Basic hygiene like handwashing and dental care
options.D: Chronic disease pharmacology and medication doses

explanation: Correct! Little ones benefit the most from mastering everyday self-care routines that keep common germs away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of feeding hungry children at school?

options.A: Elimination of all infectious skin diseases
options.B: Increased physical height within one week
options.C: Guaranteed automatic promotion to the next grade

explanation: You nailed it! A well-fed child has the brain energy needed to focus, answer questions, and join in class activities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h6)

question: Why are deworming tablets often given alongside school feeding programs?

options.A: Intestinal worms cause nutrient loss and anemia in children
options.B: Deworming tablets sweeten the drinking water supply
options.C: Parasites are required to help digest school meals properly
options.D: Worms prevent children from catching common cold viruses

explanation: Spot on! Worms steal important nutrients right from a child's tummy, which can cause malnutrition even if they eat good food. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h6)

question: Who acts as the main health bridge between the school, the family, and local clinics?
explanation: Correct! The school nurse handles health needs, talks with parents, and connects sick children to nearby health clinics. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h7)

question: A student with asthma starts wheezing badly during sports. What should the school nurse do first?

options.A: Send the student home immediately without any medical assessment
options.B: Tell the student to run faster to clear their airways naturally
options.C: Assess the student and administer the prescribed rescue inhaler
options.D: Wait until the end of the school day to notify the parents

explanation: You got it! The nurse needs to quickly check the student and give their emergency rescue inhaler as outlined in their care plan. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h7)
